solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Goofy type providing information

definitions.meaning: a stupid person, a fool or nitwit
slang for inside information or the low-down, as in 'give me the latest gen'

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are informal: a dimwit, and slang for the facts or inside story on something.

clue.text: Avoid fish, for white meat

parts.note: to avoid something is to duck it
the ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone skipping the fish course and choosing a pale meat instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A young duck served as food is poultry, which the setter counts as a light-coloured meat.

clue.text: Cat starts to prowl around without hesitation

indicators.note: used in the old sense of outside, so the opening letters wrap round the hesitation
the starts of the words prowl and around are their opening letters

parts.note: um is the sound of someone hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: A big cat begins its stalking walk confidently, not pausing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: P and A go round UM.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain lion or cougar of the Americas is a large wild feline.

clue.text: How Lancelot Brown landscaped his gardens?

definitions.text: How Lancelot Brown landscaped his gardens?

parts.words: How Lancelot Brown landscaped his gardens?
parts.note: the 18th-century English landscape gardener Lancelot Brown was nicknamed 'Capability' Brown, so he worked in a manner fitting that nickname

explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown designed the parks of many English country houses; the adverb formed from his nickname describes his work.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means competently or skilfully, a pun on the nickname of the famous gardener.

clue.text: Church artist carrying a minute photographic device

indicators.note: the church holds the other letters inside it as it carries them

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter in a church holding a tiny camera for taking pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' makes the church wrap round A and M; RA (Royal Academician) is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument that takes photographs is the obvious photographic apparatus.

clue.text: Tight-fisted type mischievously assaulting a named girl?

definitions.meaning: a miser who hates to spend money
someone who gives a playful nip to a girl called Penny

explanation.definitionFit: A stingy person who counts every coin; the second reading takes the phrase literally as one who nips a girl named Penny.

clue.text: Wave horse's feeding-bowl?

parts.note: bran is a cereal husk fed to horses
a dish is a shallow bowl

explanation.surface: An instruction to wave around the bowl a horse eats from.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish or wave something about, especially a weapon, in a threatening way.

clue.text: Child's toy bringing greetings from America

indicators.note: the plural greetings asks for the hello twice over, one copy per greeting

parts.note: yo is the American slang hello, so a greeting from America is this word

explanation.surface: A toy that arrives with good wishes from the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool that runs up and down a string is a classic plaything for kids.

clue.text: Rich dairy product: Charlie somehow created first of many

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool, as is a clot

indicators.note: the letters of created are put together in some other way
the first letter of many is taken

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie has somehow invented a luxurious dairy treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is not the NATO C here but slang for an idiot, CLOT. 'somehow' turns CREATED into TEDCREA.
explanation.definitionFit: The thick Devon and Cornwall topping for scones is a very rich product made from milk.

clue.text: Like free tickets — reciprocal, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the clue says the word for reciprocal is heard, not spelt

parts.note: complementary things complete or mirror each other, mutually supplying what the other lacks

explanation.surface: Describing free tickets as given in return for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words differ only in an E and an I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickets handed out free of charge are described as given gratis by way of courtesy.

clue.text: Sailor leaves dessert unfinished

indicators.note: the last letter of the pudding word is left off, so it is not complete

parts.note: a tart is a pastry dessert

explanation.surface: A seaman walks away without finishing his pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar is an old nickname for a seaman, and the short form is crossword stock.

clue.text: Small picture of trendy group

parts.note: in means fashionable
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A little photograph of a fashionable crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A small illustration placed within a larger one, as on a map or page.

clue.text: A tree was diseased: it comes and goes in waves

definitions.text: it comes and goes in waves

indicators.note: a diseased thing is disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sick tree that seems to sway back and forth like the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean's salty liquid is what rolls in and out with each breaker and tide.

clue.text: Install a petty officer overcome by drink?

indicators.note: the officer is enclosed by the drink, as if swallowed up by it

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer
PO is the abbreviation for petty officer in the navy

explanation.surface: Should a naval officer be put in post when he is the worse for drink?
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome by' means swallowed up, so the officer sits inside the drink, not on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone is to put them formally into a job or office.

clue.text: Most of the conflict Edward foiled

indicators.note: all but the final letter of the word the is used

parts.note: taken as written before its end is trimmed
war is armed conflict
Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward frustrated most of the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last letter of THE, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: To be blocked or frustrated in one's plans; the clue's past participle matches.

clue.text: Relative giving graduate £1,000 for a start

indicators.note: the money comes first, at the start, before the graduate

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A family member hands a new graduate a thousand pounds to get started.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is a family member, two generations up.

clue.text: A worry, containing extremely serious attack

indicators.note: the outer pieces hold the extremes inside them

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or worry someone

indicators.note: the outermost letters of serious are taken

explanation.surface: A worry that includes a very grave assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outer letters of serious, and 'containing' puts them between A and the worry.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to set upon violently, a verb meaning attack.

clue.text: Natural skill, say? Not by any means

indicators.note: say tells us the skill phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: know-how is practical skill or expertise

explanation.surface: Questioning whether innate talent is enough, and answering that it is not at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect or informal adverb meaning in no way whatsoever.

clue.text: Bag originally sold at chemist's

indicators.note: originally points to the initial letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A bag that was first sold in a pharmacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouch-like cavity or bag in a plant or animal, as in a pouch of fluid.

clue.text: Record one's held in the Washington area

indicators.note: one's letters are held inside the district

parts.note: DC, the District of Columbia, is the area of the US capital
one's is read as one is, I and IS shortened to IS

explanation.surface: A record held somewhere in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is I + S, one plus the 's of 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record or CD is a flat round recording, and the words are used interchangeably.

clue.text: Breach that sounds complete

indicators.note: sounds indicates a word heard the same as the one for complete

parts.note: whole means complete or entire

explanation.surface: A gap in a wall that seems to be finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a gap or opening made in a wall or defences.

clue.text: Similarly affected, like the Owl and the Pussy-Cat

definitions.meaning: facing the same difficult situation as others

definitions.text: like the Owl and the Pussy-Cat
definitions.meaning: in Edward Lear's nonsense poem the two animals went to sea together in a pea-green vessel

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes people sharing the same predicament; Lear's two animals literally shared one vessel.

clue.text: Chewy sweet a king fed to beast of burden

indicators.note: the letters go inside the animal, as food is fed into it

parts.note: a camel carries loads
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch giving a toffee to his pack animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed to' puts AR inside CAMEL, after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A toffee-like confection made from boiled sugar and butter.

clue.text: Youth holding end of poodle's leash

indicators.note: the young man's letters surround the picked letter

parts.note: a lad is a young man

indicators.note: the final letter of poodle is taken

explanation.surface: A boy holds the end of a poodle's lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives E, which 'holding' puts inside LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The strap or cord a dog walker holds goes by this British word as well as the American one.
